blocks.x: Louie Armstrong and all these different musicians, but did you ever play the banjo? I know you used to sell banjo mutes. They talk about that. Yeah. You kept all different kind of accessories, huh?
In my store you could get anything you wanted, see. You see, Dick, here's the dip. You got this on and on?

It is. Dick, you see, this is the thing. I was a musician. I come from musical families from way back, see. You get kind of, you don't look for the dollar sign. All right. Let's see. Now, yeah, I'm trying to think of, oh gee, well, you see. Think of some of them guys, man. Gee whiz. Yeah, there was a, well, we used to call this a tone control, a tone control, see. And you could raise it, you know, a lot closer you'd put it to the band, the bridge, you know, the moment before the sound would get. Oh, what's the fella's name that used to come on then and I used to have to run him out there and taking his hat off all the time when he was coming there, the banjo player.
Oh, not the one that used to go on up about reeds.

Oh, no, that was John Casimir. Funny thing talking about John Casimir. You know John Casimir. Sure. John Casimir used to use plastic reeds, see. And no matter, any reed I ever got, I used to have to have, I had a special reed, not a special reed, but a reed cutter just for him, for his reeds, see. I used to have to always cut, he'd say to me, they won't play unless you cut part of that reed off for me. Come on, John Casimir. And he called up my wife and said, well, you know, she'd call him and tell him when I got his reeds in or something like that. But any kind of a set, you name it, we had it. We had anything for instruments. Now I remember when John Schaaf was taken from, oh that's the guy I first sent John in there, played with George E. Lewis, the banjo player. Lawrence Moreira. Lawrence Moreira. Yeah. Lawrence Moreira used to send a lot of fellas over for those tone controls, you know. And that's the first time I met John Schaaf when he was real young, you know. And of course John and we were very, very friendly all the way, you know.
